chitchat: "Every camera is a choice the Architect made about who to watch. We make choices back."
"We don't want to burn the city down. We want the keys to it. There's a difference, and it's everything."
"Paper doesn't leak. Paper doesn't get hacked. Paper is why we're still here."
description: A tall woman with cropped iron-grey hair, standing at the great hand-drawn wall map with a grease pencil behind one ear. She has the calm of someone who plans in years, not days. When she looks at you it's not unkind, but it's complete: she's deciding what you're good for, and she's usually right.

asc_accept.text: "Green line will start you at Halcyon. Eyes open, mouth shut." She picks the pencil back up. "Come and tell me what breathes out there."

asc_after.text:
"Dig carefully. A door that opens for you out there opens for a reason, and the reason isn't you."

She is already marking the western edge of the map, a shape she doesn't have a symbol for yet.

asc_offer.text:
"Start at the source. The claims hall in Halcyon Towers. Watch where the payouts route, and then follow the track west until it stops being grass."

A beat.

"I don't know what's out there. That's exactly why I want eyes that'll come back."

options.label: There's a whole complex out there.

asc_report.text:
She listens to all of it without moving.

"A chrome city. Turrets. A Gate that turns you away."

She exhales slowly.

"So that's where the money has been going. Whatever that place is, it's the machine's friend and not ours."

A long look, and she doesn't soften it.

"Learn what it is, if you're going back. But Halcyon. Don't ever trust a payout from them again."

"Did anybody take your name?"

asc_reveal.text:
Cyrelle sets down the grease pencil, which is rare.

"Bothering me too. Halcyon settles its biggest claims by moving money west, past the grass, off every map we keep. Insurance doesn't work like that. Insurance argues. Insurance delays. Something out there's wearing Halcyon's face and it has never once argued a claim."

She studies you.

"You have earned enough rope to go and pull on it. Quietly. Find out what's west, and don't let them learn you're Watch."

blind.text:
"That's the long game. It's slow, and it's the only one worth playing."

She doesn't smile yet.

"Do the arithmetic before you decide you're impressed. There are sixty-one of us. On the other side there's a machine that owns every wire in the Basin, and a chrome city out west that can print a new body faster than we can bury an old one. Nobody sensible takes that bet. I want you to know that I know it."

Now the smile, and it's thin, and it's real.

"But a machine has to be told where to look. That's the one thing it has never been able to do for itself. So we don't win this with a bomb. We win it one dark corner at a time, until the map is more ours than his, and one morning it goes looking for us and finds a city with rooms of its own again."

bye.text: "Stay sharp." She turns back to the map, already somewhere else.

options.label: How long have you been sitting here?
Say what you came to say.

cross_meet.text:
She doesn't put a light on. She's on the stool by the type cases with her coat still buttoned, and she has clearly been there a while, and she isn't surprised.

"Six nights," she says. "Halloran said four. I said seven. It was six."

She doesn't get up.

"Sit down. You have had a long walk and you're going to have a longer one back."

cross_meet2.text:
"Here is what I'm not going to do. I'm not going to tell you that you have made a terrible mistake, because you know, and being told is what makes a person dig in."

She nods at the press behind her.

"Take the address. Genuinely, take it. It's a machine and we have two more, and the day they come for it's the day we find out how many of them are prepared to be seen carrying a crate out of a basement."

A long pause, and she isn't performing it.

"But you're still on the rota. Nobody has crossed you off. That isn't sentiment. Crossing somebody off is a decision, and I'm not making it while there's any version of this where you come back."

cross_open.text:
"Nothing you would have to do tonight." She says it carefully, having rehearsed it, and not wanting it to sound rehearsed.

"You would have to still be a person we could reach. That's all it's at this stage, and I'm aware of exactly how much I'm asking for and how little I'm offering back."

She stands, finally, and pulls her coat straight.

"Go on. He'll want it before morning, and you shouldn't be the last one out of this building."

cross_refuse.text:
She takes it better than you were braced for.

"All right."

She moves off the stool to let you past the type cases, and she's careful not to touch you doing it, and that's the part you'll remember.

"For what it's worth, and it's worth nothing: I don't think you're a coward and I don't think you were bought. I think you did the arithmetic and got the right answer."

She sits back down in the dark.

"I have done it too. I just couldn't make myself live in it."

l13_done.text:
She hears the whole of it without interrupting once, which she doesn't do.

"Running." Cyrelle says it before you have finished. "The ports are capped clean and recent and he hasn't asked us for a single thing. Somebody sent would have asked for something by now. They always do, inside a week."

She turns back to the map. "He comes in. He sleeps in the commons for a month and doesn't go past the spine, and in a month I'll still be the one who decided it."

options.label: And if I can't tell which?

l13_offer.text:
"There's a boy at the Threshold." Cyrelle doesn't leave the map. "Nineteen, Spire haircut, two capped ports in his forearms, and Rennick won't turn him away and won't let him in, which is exactly the right answer and is also not an answer."

"Sit with him. He's one of three things: sent, running, or lost."

l13_take.text: "Take him something to eat. He hasn't asked for anything, which is the part I don't like." Back to the map. "And don't tell him you have been up there. Let him say it all first."

l13_why.text: "Then you tell me that." She looks up. "Don't decide. Listen, then tell me. I'll decide, and if it's wrong it'll be my fault, and I want it to be my fault. That's what this chair is."

l14_done.text:
She reads the file, then the count, then the file again.

"A whole bank of them dry." Cyrelle sits down, which is new. "Nine years of arguing about whether they would ever open the vats to everybody, and it turns out they could not, and haven't been able to for some time, and are still selling it every Tuesday to somebody like Halbrook."

A long pause. "This doesn't go in the room yet. I need to know what to do with it before forty people know I have it."

l14_offer.text:
"Nine years this room has argued about how many tanks are down there." Cyrelle puts one finger on the Spire and leaves it. "Nine years, because nobody has ever counted them. Everything we know about the vats we know from people who were being shown round."

"Count them. Bring a file that says so."

l14_take.text: "Hall first, Registry after, and out of the building before anybody has a reason to look at you twice." She's already back on the map. "You have a face they let in. It's the only thing about your last year I'm glad of."

l14_why.text:
"They are." She doesn't soften it. "That's exactly why I want the number. A promise you haven't counted is a poster."

She takes the finger off the map. "And if the number is good, I want to know that too, and I'll say so in this room, and half of them won't forgive me for it."

l15_done.text:
She takes the chip, looks at it once, and puts it in her coat.

"No name." Cyrelle nods slowly. "Good. You'll work out whose it's inside a fortnight, if you haven't already, because it isn't difficult and there are only forty of us."

She holds your eye for a moment. "And then you'll be the second person carrying it. I'm sorry about that. It's the actual price and nobody warns anybody about it."

l15_offer.text:
She takes you out of the ops room to say it, which she has never done.

"Somebody here has been taking money. Eleven days I have known and I haven't said a name to anybody, including Halloran, including you." Cyrelle keeps her voice at the level of a conversation about rations. "The drop is behind the tap. I want the money. Tonight."

l15_take.text: "Behind the tap, low on the left, and don't look round while you're doing it." She's already going back in. "Bring it to me and say no name. Not even if you know it. Especially not then."

l15_why.text:
"I want the person to find an empty gap and understand that it's over and that nobody is coming." She folds her arms. "They'll stop. People do, when the money stops and nothing else happens. It's the nothing else that does it."

"If I take them out of the bunkroom at three in the morning I have forty people who sleep worse for a year and one person who's gone. I have done that. It isn't better."

map.text:
"Every red mark is one of the Architect's eyes." She sweeps a hand across the east of the Basin. "Every one struck through is an eye we have closed."

"It looks like a small thing, one camera. It's not. A blind spot is a place people can breathe, and meet, and move, and a place the machine has to guess about. String enough of them together and you have something it can't see at all."

"You have a city with rooms of its own again."

ret_accept.text:
"Then go and get her."

She marks the Vats on the wall, and for once it isn't a red eye. It's a circle.

"Two rules and I'm not flexible on either. You don't put a floor supervisor in the ground. Kill one of Halcyon's middle managers and by morning we didn't rescue a witness, we murdered a man in a polo shirt, and every name on that slate turns into paperwork nobody will ever read. Cosh them, lock them in a cupboard, walk around them. I don't care which."

She looks up.

"And you come back at her pace. Not yours. She's carrying everything she is and she can't run with it. If you get here without her, don't get here."

"Can you carry somebody who can't walk?"

ret_after.text:
"Eleven thousand and forty." She says the number the way you would test a weight. "Every one of them a policy somebody's mother is still paying into. That isn't a cult out there. That's a debt collector with a chapel."

She looks past you at the woman on the crate.

"She keeps the room. She keeps the name. Anybody asks, she's Watch now, and the Watch don't file people."

ret_offer.text:
"I told you the first day there would be work. Cameras to close. Its little servants to inconvenience."

She finally turns all the way round.

"And people to move out from under the machine's eye. That's the one I have never been able to hand anybody, because we have never had somebody inside worth moving."

"Now we do. And she found us."

ret_offer2.text:
"A sub-registrar in the Vats. Nine years filing the accounts they stopped paying to run."

A short breath.

"She isn't a defector. She's a clerk who read her own filing cabinet and couldn't stop reading it. She'll hand us the whole archive. She won't do it from inside that building, and she can't get out of it on her own."

ret_report.text:
Cyrelle looks at the woman sitting on a crate in her bunker, and then at the slate, and then at the woman again, and she takes the slate second.

"Nine years." She doesn't say it to you. "Nine years of writing down who they were never going to bring back, and filing it, and coming in the next day."

She thumbs the archive open, reads for a while, and her face does something Halloran wouldn't believe if you told him.

"You understand what this is. It isn't proof they're a cult. Nobody cares about a cult. It's proof an insurer is selling a resurrection it has already decided not to perform."

options.label: There's more. They keep the ones who lapse.

ret_reveal.text:
She sets the grease pencil down and this time she doesn't pick it back up.

"Say the last part again."

You do. Cyrelle stands very still in front of a map covered in eyes she has spent her life closing.

"So the payouts weren't going west to somebody. They were going west to themselves."

A flat sound that isn't a laugh.

"An insurance company that owns the afterlife it's underwriting. No wonder they never argue a claim."

options.label: There's a boy at the Threshold.
Nobody has ever counted the tanks.
(she's sitting in the dark by the press)
What does the Watch actually want?
Something about Halcyon has been bothering me.
I climbed the Spire. Halcyon is them.
She's here. She's standing right there.

root.text:
She doesn't turn from the map at first.

"New blood. Halloran vouches for you, and Halloran isn't generous with that."

Now she looks.

"I'm Cyrelle. I run operations down here, which is to say I decide, most days, what the Architect gets to see next. Sit with that a moment, and then tell me what you want to know."

work.text:
"There will be operations for you soon enough. Cameras to close. People to move out from under the machine's eye. Its little servants to inconvenience."

She taps the map.

"For now, get the lie of the place. Talk to the Quartermaster. Rest while you can. When there's a run with your name on it you'll hear about it."

clothing_layers: a long field coat, collar up, dead-grey

name: Cyrelle
